# This was materially smaller than the proposal's 2026-09-04 manual-sample
# estimate (~49 candidate false-negatives out of ~227 registry-wide false
# entries). The proposal explicitly anticipated the drift ("the exact
# counts... will have moved; re-verify before acting") and that estimate
# was a manual sample, not a claim of precision -- so the gap was not
# treated as an error in either number, and the 2026-09-04 estimate is left
# as historical record rather than corrected.
# reference rewritten from $REPO_ROOT/bubbles/<path> to the equivalent
# reads_working_tree()'s match set -- and now carry closureComplete: true.
# Each was re-run standalone (zero behavior change) and shellcheck-clean
# before and after. The dependency this unlocked for
# proven load-bearing by execution: moving it aside made the selftest FAIL
# CLOSED (exit 1, "adapter exists ... not found"), not silently pass or
# skip, satisfying this proposal's fail-closed acceptance bar; the file was
# restored and reconfirmed byte-identical and passing.
# were investigated and deliberately LEFT UNFIXED: their triggering
# references point outside bubbles/ (agents/, docs/, or BUGS.md at the repo
# root), which needs a DOUBLE $SCRIPT_DIR/../../<path> hop. normalize_ref()
# in generate-validation-checks.sh only collapses a SINGLE `dir/../` hop (its
# own comment says so); tracing a double hop through it produces a wrong,
# non-existent path, so the reference would be silently DROPPED from the
# tracked closure rather than correctly re-pointed -- reintroducing exactly
# the staleness this proposal exists to remove, and worse than leaving the
# false-negative alone. Fixing this needs either a normalize_ref() multi-hop
# fix (shared derivation logic -- shape (b), out of scope here) or a
# different per-file approach; recorded as an open follow-up rather than
# forced through with a regression. This file's counts (155 total false
